Subject: MAP kickoff + sequencing ask

Tom — great to meet yesterday. As discussed, I attached a first-pass mutual action plan (Redwood-MAP-v1.xlsx) that maps evaluation milestones to procurement and legal gates. High level asks to get us to signature: 

- Confirmation of target go-live window (you mentioned early Aug)
- Procurement lead and expected PO timing (invoice vs PO)
- Legal contact for DPA redlines and any required exec approvals
- Security artifacts (SOC2 report, enclave details) we should surface to your team

Proposed sequencing in the MAP: evaluation -> pilot/PO -> MSA & DPA concurrent review -> order form + payment -> pilot start. That order means we can lock order form pricing while legal completes DPA redlines, but happy to flip the MSA/DPA order depending on your procurement needs.

Can you loop in the procurement and legal folks and confirm the gating items + a 3–4 week window for legal? Marcus and Laura are on cc to help with the DPA/MSA templates and to agree on a final timeline.

Thanks — Stephanie
-- 
Stephanie Nguyen

Stephanie — thanks for the summary and the MAP. Quick answers from procurement side: target go-live is Aug 9 (internal product launch), procurement needs a signed order form + PO by Jul 20 to hit that. Procurement prefers MSA signed before issuing PO; DPA can be signed in parallel but needs to be reviewed early so we can attach it to the PO.

Action items from our side:
- I will introduce Sarah (legal) and procurements@bioquant.ai (who I cc'd).
- We will aim to review DPA redlines within 2 weeks of receiving a proposed redline document.
- SOC2 report or equivalent is required before PO creation; if Redwood can provide a short security packet that speeds the review.

Does Redwood typically accept MSA with signature blocks held open for order forms? If not, we can adjust sequencing on our side but prefer MSA before PO.

Tom

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + sequencing ask — DPA redlines attached

Stephanie / Marcus — attaching DPA-redlines-bioquant_2026.pdf with our requested changes. High-level notes:

- Data scope: tighten definition of "Customer Data" to exclude aggregated telemetry and explicitly call out PHI is out of scope.
- Subprocessing: require prior written consent for new subprocessors and 30-day notice for changes.
- Security obligations: include SOC2 Type II or equivalent attestation; conditional clause for on-prem deployments.
- Liability / indemnity: we need clarification on limits and carveouts for regulated data.

To keep to Tom's Jul 20 PO ask, we'll need a 10 business day turnaround on DPA redlines from Redwood and a security packet (SOC2 + architecture diagram). If Redwood can accept our minor MSA edits we can move to signature and issue PO immediately after.

Please confirm you received the redlines and estimated turnaround.

Thanks — Sarah

Team — thanks for the inputs. Attached is MAP-final-20260602.xlsx which incorporates Sarah's redlines as action items and a proposed sequencing that meets BioQuant's PO date without blocking legal review. Key milestones and ownership: 

1) 2026-06-04 — Redwood to submit DPA response (Marcus) + security packet (Dev)
2) 2026-06-09 — BioQuant returns counter-redlines (target)
3) 2026-06-18 — MSA final negotiated (signature-ready)
4) 2026-07-15 — Order form final + DocuSign ready
5) 2026-07-20 — PO issued by BioQuant
6) 2026-08-09 — Pilot / go-live

Notes / sequencing logic: we will circulate an MSA with our standard commercial terms while we handle DPA redlines in parallel; if BioQuant requires MSA signature first, we can flip steps 3 and 5 but that risks delaying PO. The MAP has two lanes: "MSA-first" and "MSA-parallel" with owners and SLAs. Please confirm which lane you prefer by EOD Jun 9 so we can lock the DocuSign envelope (link below).
